examples.problem: Let ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14046753/assets/e199e48633dbaeeb817da846163a9c8a9bf1ae3355c69b56461b25a13ef73406.png) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14046753/assets/4ce6e454ff96976ddeb735d1ab42562fe3b7eb16f16e7c0402d8040f9586907b.png). Find the vector projection of $\mathbf{a}$ onto $\mathbf{b}$.
examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+0\cdot 5+1\cdot (-1)}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{0}{{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}b \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Let $c=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]$ and $d=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 5\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $d$ onto $c.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{c}\,d & =\frac{c\cdot d}{c\cdot c}c \\  & =\frac{{c}_{x}{d}_{x}+{c}_{y}{d}_{y}+{c}_{z}{d}_{z}}{{c}_{x}^{2}+{c}_{y}^{2}+{c}_{z}^{2}}c \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 2+1\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot 5}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}c \\  & =-\frac{14}{14}⟨2,1,-3⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
